- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid missing downward momentum.
- If model shows a sharp spike in forecast (e.g., >5% above recent mean), reduce by 2–5% in next period to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days deviating from 30d moving average), model often fails to correct; apply a 1–3% downward bias in next forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment-driven momentum, not just historical trend.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 5 days, model often misjudges direction; use sentiment transition as trigger for 1–2 day correction in forecast direction.
